facts.text: For the DOTE Permit & License Center, the city directs visitors to take an elevator to floor four, turn right and follow the hall toward Central Avenue; the office is opposite the back stairwell. The page does not identify a step-free entrance or confirm elevator operation.
facts.quote: Upon entering City Hall, take the elevators to the fourth floor. Turn right out of the elevator and proceed down the hallway toward the back of the building nearest Central Avenue. The Permit & License Center is opposite the back stairwell.

facts.text: The City Hall welcome page lists public building hours as Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–5 p.m. Check the hours of the particular office you need.
facts.quote: City Hall is located at 801 Plum St., in Downtown Cincinnati. It is open to the public Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

facts.text: DOTE lists its Permit & License Center in Suite 425, Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–4 p.m. Its opening time differs from the building welcome page; confirm entry before an early visit.
facts.quote: DOTE Permit & License Center City Hall 801 Plum Street Suite 425 Cincinnati, Ohio 45202 Monday through Friday 8:00 a.m. – 4:00 p.m.

facts.text: The building directory places the Mayor and City Manager on floor one, the Treasurer and bill payments on floor two, and Council Chambers and the Clerk of Council on floor three. Confirm your destination before travelling.
facts.quote: First Floor Mayor's Office City Manager's Office Human Relations Commission Real Estate/Family Relocation BLOC Coffee & Sandwich Shop Second Floor Law Retirement Treasurer's Office Pay All Bills Vendors & Peddlers License Third Floor Council Chambers Council Member's Offices Clerk of Council

facts.text: The city says it generally provides communication aids on request. Contact the Office of Aging and Accessibility for communication support; this is a citywide policy, not a list of equipment installed in Council Chambers.
facts.quote: The City will generally, upon request, provide appropriate aids for effective communication for qualified individuals with disabilities. Please contact the City’s Office of Aging and Accessibility if you require any special accommodations or communication aids.

facts.text: For assistance at a city meeting or event, the city asks for an accommodation request three to five business days ahead. Its policy links an online request and lists the ADA Compliance Office at 513-352-5361.
facts.quote: If you need assistance in participating in a meeting or event due to a disability as defined under the Americans with Disabilities Act, please contact the City’s ADA Compliance Office at least three (3) to five (5) business days prior to the scheduled meeting or event to request an accommodation.

facts.text: The council registration page offers remote participation or written comments. Remote registration may be sent up to a week ahead and is due by 2 p.m. the previous day; for public-hearing items, the posted deadline is 9 a.m. on the hearing day. Staff follow up by email or phone.
facts.quote: This registration form can be submitted up to one week prior to the meeting but must be received by 2:00 p.m. the day before you are requesting to participate, with the exception that registration forms for public hearing items will be accepted if received by 9:00 a.m. the day of the hearing. Once you submit your form, someone from the Office of the Clerk of Council will contact you with additional information by e-mail and/or by phone.

facts.text: In-person public-comment registration can be completed in Council Chambers before the scheduled meeting. Contact the Clerk of Council at 513-352-3246 with participation questions.
facts.quote: Registration for in person public comment can be completed in Council Chambers prior to the scheduled meeting.

facts.text: A basic group tour lasts about one hour; the tour with a simulated council meeting lasts about one and a half hours. The tour page asks for at least two weeks’ notice through 513-591-6000. Rest breaks and seating along the tour are not described.
facts.quote: A basic tour lasts approximately 1 hour, and a tour with a simulated City Council meeting lasts approximately 1½ hours.

facts.text: CRC lists Mt. Auburn as an indoor, year-round warm-water pool. This does not establish a particular water temperature or uninterrupted daily opening.
facts.quote: Mt. Auburn Pool Indoor (Year Round) Mt. Auburn 2034 Young Street Cincinnati, Ohio 45219 Rectangular Standard Pool, Warm Water

facts.text: Pool memberships can be bought online or at the pool and last twelve months from purchase. CRC says pool programs such as lessons and water exercise require a pool membership.
facts.quote: Pool memberships will be available for purchase both online and at the pool and are valid 12 months from purchase date. Pool programs (i.e. Swim Lessons, Water Exercise) require a pool membership.

facts.text: The pool page links separate fall and December program schedules. Check the current timetable for open-swim sessions and program dates before travelling.
facts.quote: Fall PROGRAM SCHEDULE dECEMBER SCHEDULE

facts.text: For pool questions, call 513-381-6780; the published weather hotline is 513-352-4033. The separate CRC Aquatics Office is 513-357-7665.
facts.quote: Pool Phone: 513-381-6780 CRC Aquatics Office: 513-357-POOL (7665) Mt. Auburn Pool Weather Hotline: 513-352-4033

facts.text: CRC’s systemwide inclusion program lists adaptive equipment and assistance with daily activities among possible accommodations. Request an Accommodation and Assessment Form at registration. This does not confirm specific pool equipment, transfer assistance or an approved individual arrangement at Mt. Auburn.
facts.quote: Types of Accommodations Changes in Rules and/or Policies Assistance with ADLs (activities of daily living) Architectural Changes Adaptive Equipment Increased Supervision Behavior Supports Specialized Training for Staff Boardmaker Tools for Communication

facts.text: CRC’s systemwide inclusion program lists Boardmaker communication tools among possible accommodations. Ask for an Accommodation and Assessment Form at registration; availability at this pool is not established.
facts.quote: If you feel an accommodation would be beneficial or necessary, please request an Accommodation and Assessment Form at the time of registration at the recreation center.

facts.text: The branch posts all-day closures for staff development on November 13, 2026, and Thanksgiving on November 26–27. The same page advertises a November 13 used-book sale; confirm any event-specific admission rather than assuming normal library service.
facts.quote: Staff Development Day Friday, November 13, 2026 Closed All Day Thanksgiving and Friday After Thursday, November 26, 2026 - Friday, November 27, 2026 Closed All Day

facts.text: The district FAQ names Independence as a drive-through pickup and return location. It says drive-through hours follow branch hours; the one-hour-early exception is specifically for Erlanger. No curbside service is currently offered.
facts.quote: What are the hours of the drive thru? The drive thru is open when the branch is open. Erlanger closes one hour before the branch.

facts.text: The district FAQ says telescopes cannot be checked out or returned through the drive-through; those transactions require going inside.
facts.quote: At this time we are unable to check out or accept returns of our telescopes through the drive-thru. You must come inside the branch.

facts.text: The district FAQ says a ready hold is kept for three days, with notification by the chosen phone, text or email method. Check that notice before making a pickup trip.
facts.quote: How long is a hold held for me? Your hold will be held for three days. Print This Answer How will I know when my hold is ready for pickup? When your hold is ready, we will contact you via your preferred method: phone, text, or email.

facts.text: Family members may collect holds with the borrower’s library card number, according to the district FAQ. This does not establish special pickup hours or an exception to the telescope rule.
facts.quote: Can family members pick up my holds? Yes, they can pick up your holds if they have your library card number.

facts.text: The homebound service is for Kenton County residents who have short- or long-term disabilities, mobility limitations or other barriers to visiting. The district invites requests through its homebound page; eligibility and delivery arrangements need staff confirmation.
facts.quote: Homebound Delivery service is designed to offer library materials to Kenton County residents who may face short or long-term disabilities, mobility limitations, or other barriers that make visiting a traditional library location difficult.
